title: Login screen
description: The sign-in screen as the reference composition for a whole screen built from the contract, in two parts the route arranges: LoginCard, a glass Card (the pane) floating on the FullBleedCanvas, and LoginForm, two required Inputs and a stacked CardFooter of primary Sign in, an or-divider, a secondary SSO button, a slotted tertiary link and fine print. The route fills the card's header from Card's own parts (the wordmark as the title, a one-line lede) and places the form under it. One composition for phone and desktop: the card is 80% of the canvas up to 30rem, and takes the width but a gutter below 40rem.

anatomy.description: The house Card in its glass variant (data-slot="card", data-variant="glass"): 80% of the canvas up to 30rem, centred by the canvas, with children. Its module gives the card's header 2rem below and sizes an svg inside the title to 60% of the width, so a wordmark can stand where the text would.
Composed by the route from Card's parts: CardTitle carrying the Juniper wordmark (the svg from src/assets, currentColor) over a one-line CardDescription lede.

react-aria Form with native validation: isRequired blocks the submit, the first empty field takes focus and FieldError shows the message; onSubmit hands the credentials to the caller. Centred at 22rem.

Email Input (type email, autocomplete username, autoFocus) and Password Input (autocomplete current-password). Nothing user-scoped: which workspaces exist is an answer the API gives after sign-in, so no workspace picker before it (component-architecture §6.4).

Stacked: the primary submit, an or-divider, the secondary Continue with SSO button (only with onSingleSignOn), the slotted secondaryAction (a discrete Button asChild around a router Link) and the fine print.

usage: A reference composition, not a reusable primitive: copy the structure (FullBleedCanvas as the ground, a glass Card centred on it, the header from Card's parts, the form from Field-composed controls) rather than the components.

The route arranges: <FullBleedCanvas><LoginCard><CardHeader>…</CardHeader><LoginForm … /></LoginCard></FullBleedCanvas>. The card's title and lede are the route's words (or its wordmark); the form's fine print is the form's own.
Render it on FullBleedCanvas: the card's width and its narrow rule are relative to the canvas (@container full-bleed-canvas), and the route needs no CSS of its own.

Controlled: onSignIn({ email, password }) is all the form reports and the component never navigates; the route decides where a sign-in lands. Ask for nothing user-scoped before sign-in (workspaces, names, plans): the authenticated shell resolves those once it knows who signed in.
Pass onSingleSignOn (no arguments) to render the SSO button; leave it out and the divider goes with it. Pass the guest or sign-up link as secondaryAction so the router stays in the route.
The card wears glass because it floats on a ground (theming §4.6); the form lives on it because the extruded controls only read on a bark-50 surface. Never move fields onto the ground.
Validation is react-aria's native behaviour; do not add noValidate or an attempted-submit flag. Messages come through errorMessage on each Input.
The ground, its photograph, grain and credit come from FullBleedCanvas; change them there, never in this module.
